restrictions: Llama 3.2 Community License: redistribution requires including the agreement, displaying 'Built with Llama', and retaining the copyright notice.
Any distributed AI model created/trained/fine-tuned/improved using Llama Materials must include 'Llama' at the beginning of its name (per fetched license text).
Licensees with >700M monthly active users on the release date must request a separate license from Meta.
Use must comply with Meta's Acceptable Use Policy (https://www.llama.com/llama3_2/use-policy).

Per fetched summary of the Llama 3.2 AUP, rights under Section 1(a) are not granted to EU-domiciled individuals/companies for multimodal Llama 3.2 models; the exact scope was read via a summarizer and must be re-read from the primary text before relying on it.
Governing-law/entity terms differ by licensee location (see license text); not legal advice.
supported_formats: safetensors (HF; gated repo requires accepting license)
ExecuTorch .pte (documented, incl. Qualcomm QNN & Vulkan tutorials)
MLC LLM (prebuilt Android configs listed in third-party source)

architecture.notes: 24 attention heads, intermediate 8192 per search excerpt of a mirror config; rope scaling factor 32.

uncertainties: License/AUP read through a summarizer, not verbatim; legal review of the exact text is required before shipping a derivative.
Context length 131072 and architecture from third-party mirrors' config excerpts; official meta-llama repo is gated and was not fetched.
Whether LoRA adapters alone (without base weights) count as 'AI model' requiring the 'Llama' name prefix is not settled by the text we read - owner/legal decision.
Llama 3.2 is not Meta's newest release (Llama 4 exists); chosen because it is the small-size Llama line.
verification.method: WebFetch of primary GitHub/PyPI/apache.org documents where reachable; huggingface.co, ai.google.dev, blog.google and mistral.ai were blocked by the egress proxy, so those were seen only as search-result excerpts. Registry rule: permission fields are 'yes' only where a license identifier was supported by a primary or official-card excerpt AND the license text itself was read; otherwise 'unverified'.
